parsed.rationale: Every member declared on `AudioPlayerProtocol` (9 members: `eventStream`, `installRenderTap`, `isPlaying`, `makeAudioBufferStream`, `play`, `removeRenderTap`, `state`, `stateStream`, `stop`) appears verbatim in `TimeShiftablePlayer`, which additionally declares 6 time-shifting-specific members (`isAtLiveEdge`, `maxLookbackSeconds`, `secondsBehindLive`, `seek`, `seekToLive`, `timePositionStream`). This is a textbook strict-subset relationship: `TimeShiftablePlayer` is a specialisation of `AudioPlayerProtocol` that adds time-shift capability. Both protocols live in the same package (`Playback`) and the same directory (`Shared/Playback/Sources/PlaybackCore/Protocols/`), so no cross-package dependency is introduced. Making `TimeShiftablePlayer` inherit from `AudioPlayerProtocol` eliminates the 9 duplicated member declarations, enforces the conceptual hierarchy in the type system, and allows any site that only needs basic playback to accept an `AudioPlayerProtocol` without knowing about time-shifting.
